## Direct Answer: How to Score 160+ Marks in SSC CGL & CHSL in 90 Days

> [!IMPORTANT]  
> **Core Fact**: Scoring 160+ marks in SSC CGL / CHSL Tier-1 requires balancing 45+ marks each in English Comprehension and General Intelligence (Reasoning), while scoring 40+ in Quantitative Aptitude and 25+ in General Awareness. The key differentiator is completing 5 years of TCS Previous Year Questions (PYQs) and taking 30 full-length timed computer mock tests.

The Staff Selection Commission Combined Graduate Level (**SSC CGL**) and Combined Higher Secondary Level (**SSC CHSL**) recruit officers into premier central government departments—including the **Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), Enforcement Directorate (ED), Ministry of External Affairs (MEA), Income Tax, and Central Secretariat Service (CSS)**. With competition growing every cycle, this 90-day blueprint delivers an elite-level study framework designed for both working aspirants and full-time candidates.

---

## SSC CGL / CHSL Tier-1 Exam Pattern & Target Benchmarks

Tier-1 is a 60-minute qualifying computer-based examination featuring 100 questions for 200 marks. Each wrong attempt incurs a **0.50 mark penalty** (negative marking):

| Section | Number of Questions | Maximum Marks | Safe Target Score | Realistic Time Budget |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **General Intelligence & Reasoning** | 25 Questions | 50 Marks | **46 – 50 Marks** | 12 – 14 Minutes |
| **English Comprehension** | 25 Questions | 50 Marks | **44 – 48 Marks** | 10 – 12 Minutes |
| **Quantitative Aptitude (Maths)** | 25 Questions | 50 Marks | **40 – 46 Marks** | 25 – 28 Minutes |
| **General Awareness (GK/GS)** | 25 Questions | 50 Marks | **26 – 34 Marks** | 5 – 7 Minutes |
| **Total Composite Benchmark** | **100 Questions** | **200 Marks** | **160+ Marks** | **60 Minutes Total** |

### Sectional Weightage & Target Share
- **General Intelligence & Reasoning**: [BAR:50%:Reasoning Target (48/50 Marks)]
- **English Comprehension**: [BAR:46%:English Target (46/50 Marks)]
- **Quantitative Aptitude**: [BAR:42%:Maths Target (42/50 Marks)]
- **General Awareness**: [BAR:30%:GA Target (30/50 Marks)]

## The Topper-Approved Booklist for SSC CGL & CHSL

Do not jump between multiple resources. Rely on these industry-standard textbooks tested across successive SSC topper generations:

| Subject Domain | Standard Recommended Book | Author / Publisher | Key Focus Area & Utility |
|---|---|---|---|
| **English Grammar** | *Plinth to Paramount / English for General Competitions (Vol 1)* | Neetu Singh (KD Publication) | Explains all 120 rules of grammar in bilingual Hindi & English with targeted rule-wise exercises. |
| **English Vocabulary** | *BlackBook of English Vocabulary* | Nikhil Gupta | Exhaustive collection of One-Word Substitutions, Idioms & Phrases, and Synonyms/Antonyms asked by SSC from 1997 to present. |
| **English Practice** | *SSC English Chapterwise Solved Papers (6000+ TCS MCQs)* | Pinnacle / Kiran Publication | Perfect for practicing sentence improvement, error spotting, and cloze tests. |
| **Quantitative Aptitude** | *SSC Mathematics 6800+ TCS MCQs* | Pinnacle Publications | Categorized topic-by-topic and shift-by-shift with clean arithmetic and algebraic solutions. |
| **Maths Concept Refinement** | *Play with Advanced Maths* | Abhinay Sharma / Rakesh Yadav | Invaluable for mastering Geometry, Mensuration 3D, Trigonometry, and Coordinate Geometry. |
| **General Intelligence (Reasoning)** | *Kiran SSC Reasoning Chapterwise Solved Papers* | Kiran Institute | Contains every pattern of series, matrix, analogies, and missing number puzzles. |
| **General Knowledge** | *General Knowledge (Classic Yellow Book)* | Lucent Publication | Covers static History, Geography, Indian Polity, and General Science. |
| **Current Affairs** | *Monthly Magazines / Annual Roundups* | Parcham Classes / Eduteria / Speedy | Covers high-frequency questions on government schemes, sports awards, and summits. |

## The 90-Day Step-by-Step Execution Plan

### Month 1 (Days 1 to 30): Conceptual Core & Arithmetic Dominance
- **English**: Master 4 grammar chapters per week from Neetu Singh Vol 1 (Subject-Verb Agreement, Tenses, Pronouns, Prepositions). Memorize 30 One-Word Substitutions and 20 Idioms daily from BlackBook.
- **Quantitative Aptitude**: Cover pure arithmetic first—Percentage, Ratio & Proportion, Profit & Loss, Simple/Compound Interest, Time & Work. Solve 60 questions per day exclusively from Pinnacle PYQ book.
- **Reasoning**: Focus on high-frequency topics—Coding-Decoding, Number Series, Syllogisms, and Blood Relations. Solve 50 questions daily.
- **General Awareness**: Cover Indian Polity (Articles 1 to 51A, Fundamental Rights, President, Parliament) and Modern History (1857 to Independence).

### Month 2 (Days 31 to 60): Advanced Mathematics & Sectional Speed Drills
- **English**: Start solving 2 Cloze Tests, 2 Reading Comprehension passages, and 10 Active/Passive and Direct/Indirect speech conversions daily.
- **Quantitative Aptitude**: Transition to Advanced Mathematics—Geometry (Triangle properties, Circle tangents), Mensuration 2D/3D, Trigonometry heights & distances, and Algebra identities.
- **Reasoning**: Practice complex puzzles, Missing Number grids, Dice and Cubes, and Paper Folding/Cutting. Aim to complete 25 reasoning questions in under 13 minutes.
- **General Awareness**: Complete General Science (Biology human anatomy, Chemistry formulas, Physics units) and Indian Geography (Rivers, Mineral resources, Biosphere reserves).
- **Testing**: Take 2 sectional tests weekly for each subject to pinpoint speed bottlenecks.

### Month 3 (Days 61 to 90): Full-Length Computer Simulations & Error Log
- **Daily Full Mock Test**: Take 1 full 60-minute mock test every morning at 09:00 AM sharp to simulate the real exam hall environment.
- **Post-Mock Diagnostic (90 Minutes)**: Never close a mock without reviewing every unattempted or incorrect question. Write every forgotten vocabulary word or math formula in a dedicated 'Revision Log'.
- **Time Management Practice**: Follow the proven topper sequence during the exam:  
  1. *General Awareness* (0 to 6 mins)  
  2. *English Comprehension* (6 to 18 mins)  
  3. *Reasoning* (18 to 32 mins)  
  4. *Quantitative Aptitude* (32 to 60 mins).
- **Last 10 Days**: Stop attempting new mock tests. Re-read your entire personal Mistake Log, revise BlackBook vocabulary, and re-solve top 500 toughest maths questions.

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

### Q1: Can an average student crack SSC CGL in the very first attempt?
Yes. SSC does not test high-level research math or literature English; it evaluates standard 10th-grade calculation accuracy and foundational grammar. Average students who consistently practice 5,000+ TCS PYQs routinely outperform gifted candidates who lack speed discipline.

### Q2: What is the minimum typing speed required for SSC CGL and CHSL?
Typing is mandatory for all posts in SSC CGL (Tier-2 Module II) and CHSL. Candidates must achieve a minimum speed of 27 words per minute (WPM) in English or 22 WPM in Hindi (at least 2,000 key depressions in 15 minutes) with less than 5% errors for UR category.

### Q3: Is Tier-1 score added to the final merit list in SSC CGL?
No. Under the updated SSC CGL pattern, Tier-1 is solely qualifying in nature to shortlist candidates for Tier-2. However, achieving a high score (150+) ensures you clear high cutoffs and enter Tier-2 with supreme confidence.

### Q4: How many mock tests should I complete before the actual exam?
You should complete at least 30 to 40 full-length Tier-1 mock tests. Make sure you practice on a computer with an external mouse to simulate the actual exam center testing interface.
